text: Let's focus on on that. Now we already said that at the physical layer clearly we are considering functions that are used to transmit and receive signals, right? And we said that let's consider that our BSS works at 2.4 gigahertz. This means that the access point and all the users in the BSS will communicate, transmitting and receiving for using as portion of the frequency spectrum, the one that is, for example, around 2.4 gigahertz. Other possibilities are 5 and 6 gigahertz, but let's focus on just this portion of the spectrum. And we said there there are actually three possible channels, right? Frequency channels. Where a frequency channel is a sub portion of frequencies. Okay, that's what we said. So there are three possible. They are called channel one, six and eleven, but this is minor. You don't need to remember that. But in case you've got the atomic access point, you may want to look at the configuration of your access point and you may see that if you configure it, when working at 2.4 gigahertz, you can actually select one of these three channels. So actually you can try and play with the access point at home because this can be configured. And.
